channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent moved to a military base: Sources
item.description: Bessent is the latest administration official to move to a military base.

item.title: Greetings from Senegal, where breakdancers are competing in the Youth Olympics
item.description: Senegal's breakdancers have been practicing for their country's historic hosting of the Youth Olympic Games this month. It's the first time Africa is hosting an Olympic event.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: Biden says he wouldn't have run for a second term in 2024 if he knew he had cancer
item.description: Joe Biden says he didn't know he had cancer while he was president and wouldn't have sought a second term if he'd already been diagnosed

item.title: Teen charged in murder of Javits Frimpong, 15-year-old immigrant shot in the Bronx
item.description: The NYPD is looking for others possibly connected to the shooting.

item.title: The most hacked country in Europe? Why is France the target of so many cyberattacks
item.description: The “unprecedented” hacks of French supermarket refrigerators were the latest in a series of major cyberattacks that have made the country the most hacked in Europe, according to some analysts. Cyberattacks are on the rise globally, but why is France such a ready target?

item.title: Tens of thousands attend Polish nationalist march days afer shootings
item.description: Tens of thousands of Polish nationalist sympathisers gathered in Warsaw Wednesday for an annual Independence Day March, just days after a deadly shooting spree in Krakow that shook the country. The event is held each November 11 to commemorate the ending in 1918 of 123 years of partition by Russia, Prussia and Austria. While generally peaceful, some rallies in the pasthave been marred by clashes with police or counter-demonstrators. Philip Turle gives us his take.

item.title: Kennedy relatives join the fight against Trump's arch, alleging harm to JFK's grave
item.description: Nine members of the Kennedy family have joined the legal fight against Trump's D.C. arch, arguing it would disrupt views and cast shadows over their ancestors' graves at Arlington National Cemetery.

item.title: Tehran will strike US bases in Europe if used to attack Iran, security chief says
item.description: Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei said Wednesday that Tehran would attack US bases located in Europe if they were used to carry out bombing raids against the Islamic republic. The heavy defeat of US President Donald Trump's Republican Party in the midterm elections earlier this month seems to have pushed Washington to pull back its threats to carry out fresh strikes against Iran.

item.title: Haiti: 'We need to know the truth, but so far, it’s totally dark'
item.description: Jean-Marie Théodat, Director of the Department of Geography at University Paris, is our guest.

item.title: Violent incidents in schools as French students vow to maintain protest pressure
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron on Tuesday condemned violence against teachers andgovernment officials during nationwide street protests after an official was hit by a gasoline-filled bottle outside ​a high school ‌near Paris.

item.title: No 'certainty' man sexually touched wife advertised for sex, court told
item.description: A lack of evidence means it is not possible to prove that a defendant is guilty of abusing a woman advertised for sex by her husband, his lawyer has told a court.

item.title: British soldier charged with rape of woman in Cyprus
item.description: A British soldier has been charged with the rape of a woman serving with UK forces in Cyprus.

item.title: Brazil electoral court fines Meta $1.3 MN, sees no deliberate election bias
item.description: Jan Onoszko, our correspondent in Rio, has more.

item.title: COP31 talks in Turkey: Leaders from US, China and India skip summit
item.description: Valérie Dekimpe, our environment editor, has more.

item.title: President Macron speaks for Armistice Day commemoration ceremony
item.description: On Wednesday, Emmanuel Macron presided over his final Armistice Day ceremony in Paris.

item.title: Russia bans two French lawmakers and two journalists from entry
item.description: Moscow on Wednesday said it was banning two French journalists and two French lawmakers from entering Russia in response to Paris's expulsion of pro-Russian TV commentator Xenia Fedorova earlier this year.

item.title: Armistice Day in France: Macron honors the End of World War I
item.description: With less than six months to go before the presidential election, the 11 November commemorations have taken on a political hue. On Wednesday, Emmanuel Macron presided over his final ceremony in Paris.

item.title: Spain: General strike over housing costs before national election
item.description: Millions of Spanish workers shut down businesses and public transportation in a protest on Wednesday over housing costs that the government hopes to leverage before a national election later this month. The walkout — under the slogan “Salaries. Housing. Prices.” — was the first general strike in Spain in 14 years.

item.title: Poundland bosses meeting tonight to decide firm's future, Sky News told
item.description: The directors of Poundland are holding a board meeting this evening to decide the company's future, Sky News has been told.

item.title: WATCH: Little girl rescued after sneaker wave pulls her into Pacific
item.description: The rescue was caught on camera after a child was nearly swept out to sea by a sneaker wave along the Pacific coast.

item.title: Exclusive: EU's Kallas says US 'can't negotiate on our behalf' on lifting Russia sanctions
item.description: In an exclusive interview with FRANCE 24, the EU's top diplomat Kaja Kallas discusses the war in Ukraine, the situation in the Middle East and a possible change in US President Donald Trump's foreign policy following the US midterm elections. The former Estonian prime minister, who is now the European Union's High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, also reaffirms the EU's position as a major player on the global geopolitical stage.

item.title: Woman who stole £2k worth of drinks from one Greggs store avoids prison
item.description: A prolific shoplifter who stole more than £2,000 worth of soft drinks from one Greggs store has avoided prison.

item.title: Charlotte Gainsbourg brings pioneering French lawyer Gisèle Halimi to the screen
item.description: New French film "Women on trial" revisits the landmark case in 1972 that paved the way for abortion legislation in France. Critic Manon Kerjean tells us why performances from Charlotte Gainsbourg and Cécile de France carry this powerful courtroom drama and how its directors recreated the tension of a high-profile social and legal battle.

item.title: WATCH: Blockbuster NFL trades
item.description: ABC News’ Lara Spencer has details on the big trades, including Kirk Cousins heading to the Minnesota Vikings.

item.title: WATCH: Superhero window washers make children’s day at Omaha hospital
item.description: Patients at Children’s Nebraska were surprised by superheroes washing their windows as part of a special tradition.

item.title: Trump administration moves to drop millions from SNAP under proposal
item.description: An analysis by USDA estimates that over 6 million people could lose benefits.

item.title: Following big Democratic wins, these swing voters are looking for results
item.description: For the swing voters NPR is regularly checking in with as part of its Swing Shift series, the election results brought mixed emotions, as does the pending Democratic control of Congress.

item.title: Behind Georges Larnicol's creative spin on Breton specialty kouign-amann
item.description: From a traditional Breton specialty to an imaginative, bite-sized creation, in Entre Nous we explore how French pastry chef Georges Larnicol has reinvented the famous kouign-amann while preserving its Breton identity. He tells us what makes the pastry so special and why it is much loved around the world.

item.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to a prisoner exchange as talks end with no big breakthrough
item.description: Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a large exchange of prisoners of war. U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi led to this decision, marking the biggest humanitarian release since the war began in 2022.

item.title: UNICEF head Catherine Russell: 'We're all committed to the importance of children'
item.description: More than 50 countries, 20 non-governmental and philanthropic organisations and a series of multinational companies are pledging this week to put children's rights at the heart of their policies and actions. A pact is being agreed upon at the Paris Peace Forum, where the rights of children are taking centre stage.

item.title: House Republicans elect Jim Jordan as minority leader for the next Congress
item.description: House Republicans on Tuesday elected Jim Jordan as minority leader for the next Congress, beating Majority Leader Steve Scalise, according to multiple sources.

item.title: House tables Hegseth impeachment, effectively killing it in current Congress
item.description: Hegseth framed the effort as being directed at U.S. service members.

item.title: House Republicans consider issuing subpoena to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
item.description: Several House Republicans called for a closed-door briefing.

item.title: Aneto, one of southern Europe's largest glaciers, is melting away
item.description: Within a decade, one of the largest glaciers in southern Europe will have disappeared. Aneto, the highest peak of the Spanish Pyrenees, is melting at a spectacular rate. Its demise is another sign of global warming and has much to teach glaciologists. FRANCE 24's Maude Petit-Jové, Mathilde Lopinski and Sarah Morris report.

item.title: Patrick Bury: 'It’s going to cost a lot of money to repair the systems.'
item.description: Patrick Bury, Senior associate professor in warfare and counterterrorism at University of Bath, is our guest.

item.title: US House votes to derail impeachment of Defense Secretary Hegseth
item.description: Republicans in ​the US House ​of Representatives banded together on Tuesday ​to ‌derail ⁠aneffort to impeach ‌Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Fraser Jackson, our correspondant in Washington DC, has more.

item.title: WATCH: NYC tour helicopter makes hard landing in New Jersey
item.description: The pilot of a New York City sightseeing helicopter is being praised for pulling off a remarkable emergency landing in Bayonne, New Jersey, after the chopper’s tail rotor broke off.

item.title: Violent clashes near the Sudanese border: At least 65 dead in western Ethiopia
item.description: Tom Canetti, our correspondant in Ethiopia, has more.

item.title: UK comedian David Walliams accused of grooming and sexual harassment
item.description: PRESS REVIEW – Wednesday, November 11: Spanish and French papers discuss protests in the two countries. An investigation by The Guardian and ITV accuses comedian David Walliams of "preying on young women for sex". Finally, a Doberman sensed something was wrong with a baby. It may have saved his life.

item.title: 'Welcome Home': Peru awaits Pope Leo's emotional 'homecoming'
item.description: Pope Leo will wrap ​up his visit to Argentina on Wednesday during his 12-day South America tour, with a final event expected to draw millions, before traveling to Peru in an emotional homecoming for the first Peruvian citizen to lead the Catholic Church.

item.title: France marks Armistice Day : Macron attends commemorative ceremony
item.description: Macron attends Armistice Day commemoration ceremony at the Arc de Triomphe.

item.title: Eisenkot quickly targets Netanyahu's legacy in new Israeli parliament
item.description: Israeli ex-army chief Gadi Eisenkot and his allies launched a legislative onslaught against caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's legacy on Tuesday, as a new parliament convened in a heated first session.

item.title: EU ready for 'united response' after France blames Iran for fridge hacks
item.description: The EU said Tuesday it would look to provide a "swift and united response" after France blamed Iran for a cyberattack on hundreds of supermarket fridges.

item.title: WATCH: These NFL cheerleaders balance life in the military
item.description: On Veterans Day, ABC News' Danny New talks to two cheerleaders for the Philadelphia Eagles who've also served their country.

item.title: Threatening emails sent to thousands of schools across UK, Ireland and Italy treated as hoaxes
item.description: Threatening emails sent to thousands of schools across the UK, Ireland and Italy are being treated as hoaxes.

item.title: An Iran-backed trio is accused of plotting attacks on a U.K. base hosting U.S. jets
item.description: Iran-backed operatives have been charged over nearly 20 attacks, including a plot on a U.K. base housing U.S. troops. Separately, a U.S. soldier is held in the U.K. on Russia spying claims.

item.title: Volunteer musicians play songs for veterans who are hospitalized
item.description: Volunteer musicians play for veterans and others who are hospitalized. They're part of Musicians On Call, a group that spreads the healing power of music.

item.title: Body mass index may have misclassified millions of people in UK, researchers say
item.description: Millions of people may have been misclassified on the body mass index (BMI) scale, research has suggested.

item.title: Police address 'violent incident' claim against Russell Brand made by Jemima Goldsmith
item.description: Police have addressed an alleged "violent incident" involving Russell Brand after claims made his then-girlfriend Jemima Goldsmith.

item.title: Trump's lawsuit against BBC can go ahead, judge rules
item.description: The BBC's attempt to have Donald Trump's $10bn (£7.5bn) defamation claim thrown out has been dismissed by a Florida court.

item.title: US accuses three men of 'campaign of terror' against Jewish targets and plot against RAF Fairford
item.description: The US has accused three men linked to Iran of masterminding a "campaign of terror" against Jewish targets in the UK and Europe, as well as a thwarted plot at RAF Fairford.

item.title: Four grizzly bears killed mother and daughter in Canada
item.description: Four grizzly bears captured in Canada were responsible for killing a mother and daughter earlier this month, officials have said.

item.title: Democratic lawmakers want answers on 8-year-old Haitian boy taken into ICE custody
item.description: A group of Democratic lawmakers is seeking information from the Trump administration after an 8-year-old Haitian boy was taken into government custody last week.

item.title: Jimmy Carter's family farm to be preserved and opened to the public
item.description: The family farm where President Jimmy Carter tended peanuts, corn and sugarcane as a boy and returned throughout his life will be preserved and opened to the public

item.title: House panel rebukes DOJ's handling of Epstein case
item.description: The House Oversight Committee, in a report summarizing its 15-month Jeffrey Epstein probe, rebuked the Justice Department's handling of the Epstein case.

item.title: Ex-investigator admits depriving war crimes probe of potentially valuable information
item.description: A former senior investigating officer for the Royal Military Police has admitted depriving a war crimes investigation of potentially valuable information.

item.title: WATCH: What first responders want you to know about surviving rising waters
item.description: ABC News’ Chief Meteorologist Ginger Zee has some eye-opening demonstrations she hopes can help save lives during flash floods.

item.title: UK court overturns Trinidad and Tobago law criminalising homosexual sex
item.description: ‌Trinidad and Tobago's ‌law criminalising consensual sexual ​relations between male same-sex couples has been overturned ‌by a ​UK court.

item.title: Sophie visits refugee camps on trip to Bangladesh
item.description: Sophie has visited the Rohingya refugee camps at Cox's Bazar in Bangladesh to see the support being offered to displaced people from Myanmar.

item.title: WATCH: Officer shot 6 times celebrates wedding
item.description: Five months after Buffalo Police Officer Marc Hurst was shot six times while on duty, he celebrated a moment that once seemed far from certain: marrying his fiancee, Haley.

item.title: WATCH: Woman living the 'dream' to save foxes in need
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a woman who's on a mission to save foxes at a sanctuary in upstate New York.

item.title: Police officer dies and another seriously injured after explosion in northern Spain
item.description: One police officer has died and another has lost a leg after an explosive device detonated at the scene of a shooting in northern Spain.

item.title: California's Prop 40 'billionaires' tax' measure is rejected, AP projects
item.description: The tax was introduced in response to steep cuts to California's healthcare funding that resulted from the passage of President Donald Trump's "Big Beautiful Bill."

item.title: At least 12 killed in Bulgaria motorway pile-ups involving dozens of vehicles
item.description: At least 12 people have been killed in two motorway pile-ups in eastern Bulgaria, the country's health minister said.

item.title: FBI investigating Nvidia CEO over affair with alleged Chinese spy
item.description: Donald Trump has said the FBI is looking into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy - but insisted he is a "very honourable man".

item.title: WATCH: 'Love is Blind' season 11, Erika Kirk: Here's what's trending
item.description: ABC's Rocsi Diaz takes a look at what's buzzing, including the Netflix series reunion not holding back and Erika Kirk speaking out after Dave Chappelle joked about her husband's assassination.

item.title: WATCH: What to expect from Bills-Vikings showdown
item.description: ESPN's Cameron Wolfe helps preview the matchup.

item.title: WATCH: Inside the shadowy world of counterespionage
item.description: International Spy Museum's executive director Col. Chris Costa discusses the possible tactics the suspected Chinese spy used in the Nvidia scandal.

item.title: WATCH: Disney launches 'Make the Holidays Magic' campaign
item.description: Disney kicks off the holiday season with a new short film called, “A Disney Holiday Short: The Invisible Horse.”

item.title: France blames Iran for massive cyber attack on supermarket fridges
item.description: France has accused Iran of being behind the massive cyber attack on supermarket fridges last month.

item.title: WATCH: Trump now showing 'great level of political acumen,' former staffer says
item.description: Harrison Fields served as the White House principal deputy press secretary from January to August 2025.

item.title: At least 14 dead after boat carrying migrants found near Crete
item.description: At least 14 people have died after a boat carrying migrants was found near Crete, Greek authorities have said.
